t01.N: CrossAMI for exogenous screening (F8) is computed on the training window only, and the leakage boundary is the train_end argument since version 0.3.
t01.P: CrossAMI is computed on the training window only because scores taken over the full series let test-window values leak into exogenous screening.

t02.N: known_future_drivers takes a list of variable names, then stores the future values known at prediction time, such as calendar flags, in the forecasting config object.
t02.P: Passing a variable whose future values are not known at prediction time into known_future_drivers gives the model information it will not have in production.

t05.N: The autocovariance normalized to a Pearson correlation coefficient is what the acf helper returns, and the engineering variant without normalization was added 3 months later.
t05.P: The engineering convention of dropping the normalization does not apply when the autocovariance feeds a significance test, which needs the Pearson correlation scale.

t07.N: Numerical inflation is logged as a warning in the result object, since the multiple backends for sample-size stress testing are listed in the backends parameter of the run config file.
t07.P: If a high score persists across multiple backends and sample-size stress testing, the warning is cleared; if it collapses, the inflation was numerical and the result is discarded.

t08.N: The interval_width column holds the uncertainty attached to each forecast under this practice, and the plotting helper draws it as a degree band around the line.
t08.P: The practice of attaching uncertainty does not hold for deterministic schedule values like fixed calendar holidays, which carry no forecast error at all.

t09.N: The derived-feature profile is computed first, then the raw profile, and each lag of both profiles is stored in the data-leakage candidate table with its estimation noise.
t09.P: Such lags are treated as leakage candidates because a derived feature built from the raw series cannot hold more information about the target than the raw profile.

t10.N: Surrogates are drawn by the surrogate module, with sample size n and n_surrogates set at 200 and 99 by default since version 0.2 of the package.
t10.P: Surrogates give a series-specific noise floor, and without that floor a high AMI value at some lag cannot be told apart from chance dependence.

t14.N: The degree of uncertainty attaching to forecasts is stored as a 90% interval by default, in the interval column of the forecast frame returned by the point forecast call.
t14.P: The practice does not hold for a point forecast fed straight into an automated order rule, where the downstream system accepts a single number and ignores any interval.

t15.N: The normalization in engineering code is set by the normalize argument of the autocorrelation function, and autocovariance is its unnormalized output.
t15.P: The terms are not interchangeable in engineering code when a function returns values bounded by one, since those are normalized autocorrelations.

t16.N: Rolling-origin evaluation stores the diagnostics computed on train windows in the fold_diagnostics table, one row per fold, keyed by origin date and window size.
t16.P: Train-window diagnostics in rolling-origin evaluation give fold scores that move gradually, and a sharp jump at one fold marks leakage that the next step traces.

t17.N: The upper band and the lower band for MI are returned as band_upper and band_lower, then drawn as dashed lines in the surrogate bands plot of the report.
t17.P: The lower band stops being useless when a backend's bias pushes MI estimates below zero, since the lower band then shows how far the bias reaches.

t18.N: The robustness study pipeline writes its comparison of all configured backends against linear_residual to robustness.csv, then prints a summary table of the backends.
t18.P: Backends whose lag ranks agree with linear_residual across the robustness study pipeline are kept, and a backend that reorders the top lags is dropped from the set.

t21.N: The forecasting method is selected through the method argument, and the objectives and available data are logged since release 0.3 in the run metadata file of each run.
t21.P: When fewer than two seasonal cycles of data are available, choose a seasonal naive method; with long histories and known drivers, choose a regression-based method.
